review_notes.constraint: The pinned image has no git, so nothing executes git. The fixture is written as real loose objects using stored DEFLATE blocks, and the acceptance decodes them itself: it re-frames each stream, recomputes SHA-1, walks HEAD to ref to the parent chain to trees and blobs, enforces Git tree-entry ordering and proves the object store equals the reachable set.
review_notes.decisive_test: The reviewer performed a coherent tamper: a blob payload was rewritten, re-framed as valid stored DEFLATE with a correct Adler-32, the content copy was updated to match and every manifest digest was recomputed to agree. It still failed with object-id-mismatch, which proves SHA-1 is recomputed rather than echoed from the filename. A byte flip, a self-consistent tree misordering with cascaded ids, a deleted reachable blob and an injected orphan were all caught with distinct codes.
review_notes.mutation: The card's MUT-001 is the commit body swap with indexes and timestamps left in place. It exits 1 reporting both source-digest-divergence and MUT-001, with no vector-exit finding, so the detection is behavioural reordering rather than a missing tool. The restore is byte-identical and reproduces the same stdout digest.
review_notes.determinism: Two container runs produce an identical stdout digest, host runs under two different TMPDIRs are byte-identical, and the in-run replay uses a third. build-fixture.sh never reads the sealed repo.git, so the reproduction regenerates rather than copies.
review_notes.open_info_finding: The acceptance parses per-object type and digests from the manifest and shape-validates them without cross-checking against the decoded objects; forging one still fails through the byte-for-byte manifest regeneration comparison, so it is dead assertion surface rather than a hole.
